title: Mosaic quant kernel scheduler: head-tiling and amortized dequant pooling for mixed-precision paths
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and implement a 'Mosaic' kernel scheduler that groups attention heads into small tiles at runtime and runs mixed-precision kernels (INT8/FP8/FP16) with an amortized dequantization pool. Goal: reduce per-token dequant overhead and improve end-to-end latency for streaming decode and prefill across variable sequence lengths.
background: Current runtime selects per-layer kernel implementations independently which frequently triggers many small dequant operations when heads use different precision. This amplifies overhead on short-sequence streaming decode and prefill bursts. Existing approaches (headwise staging, cast coalescing) reduce some overhead but still pay repeated per-call allocation and memory traffic. We need a runtime-level scheduling abstraction that can: 1) group compatible heads across layers and tokens, 2) share dequantized buffers across small batches, and 3) prefer fused INT8/FP8 kernels when accuracy+latency budgets allow.
proposed_solution: Implement a scheduler that: 1) Enumerates head affinity graphs from model metadata and runtime telemetry. 2) At request ingress, forms 'mosaic tiles' -- small contiguous head subsets (configurable size 4-16) that are likely to execute the same kernel path. 3) Schedules tiles into worker frames ensuring KV cache layout favors contiguous tiling. 4) Introduces an amortized dequant pool that retains recently dequantized tile buffers for the duration of the request or for short-circuiting streaming decode. 5) Extends kernel selector with a fast path that matches tile profile -> fused kernel (INT8-fused-attn, FP8-fused-epilogue) and falls back to per-head cast only when necessary. 6) Adds telemetry counters to measure reuse rate, dequant cache hit rate, memory pressure, and latency impact.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity: scheduler adds head affinity analysis and additional bookkeeping which increases scheduler CPU usage; mitigations include sampling and heuristics.
- Memory: amortized dequant pool can increase transient memory usage; we bound pool size per-request and evict using LRU.
- Accuracy: aggressive grouping may force using lower-precision fused kernels; we include per-model precision policies and A/B rollouts.
- Portability: fusion availability differs by backend/hardware (NVIDIA vs AMD vs CPU). The scheduler will consult kernel capability registry and avoid fused paths on unsupported targets.
experiments: microbench: single-request streaming decode 1-8 tokens, measure 99th latency with and without mosaic tiles
batch microbench: 8/16/32 microbatch sizes across sequence lengths 8/32/128, capture dequant reuse rate
accuracy sweep: run standard eval set to measure delta from baseline FP16 for fused INT8/FP8 kernels
memory pressure test: stress-run on 16GB GPU to validate pool bounds and eviction behavior
ab test: enable mosaic scheduler for 10% traffic on runtime-1.28 and compare tail latencies and token cost
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end streaming decode p99 latency reduced by >=10% on int8-capable models for short sequences (<=16 tokens)
Dequant pool hit rate >= 60% in representative workloads without increasing OOM incidents
No regression >0.5% in generation quality (per model evaluation suite) for routes using fused kernels
Kernel selector correctly falls back to safe path on unsupported hardware/endpoints
Automated tests covering tile formation, pool eviction, and selector decision logic added to CI
